# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Old Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system using a phased rollout. Both systems will run in parallel (dual-write/dual-read capable) throughout the migration to allow safe rollback at any stage. The old billing system remains fully operational through all user-migration phases and is only addressed after all users have been successfully migrated and verified.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (Internal & Low-Risk Users)

**Percentage of users:** 1% (~400 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end functional testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment processing, refunds, and proration logic, with zero critical/high-severity defects open; a rollback procedure has been tested and confirmed to restore affected accounts to the old system within 1 hour.

**Description:** Migrate internal employee accounts and opted-in low-ARR (annual recurring revenue) customers. Both systems run in parallel with reconciliation jobs comparing invoices/charges generated by each system for the same accounts. Manual support review of every migrated account.

---

## Phase 2: Expanded Early Adopters

**Percentage of users:** 15% (~6,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed for a minimum of 5 business days with billing discrepancy rate below the halt threshold (see Metrics below), no unresolved P1/P2 incidents attributable to the new system, and customer support ticket volume for migrated accounts within 1.2x of baseline (non-migrated) ticket volume.

**Description:** Expand to a randomized cross-section of customers across pricing tiers and geographies (excluding highest-ARR enterprise accounts). Introduce automated reconciliation alerting. Enable customer-facing communication (email notice) 5 business days prior to each user's migration.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability Rollout

**Percentage of users:** 74% (~29,600 users), migrated in weekly waves of no more than 15% of total users per wave

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed with billing discrepancy rate below threshold for 10 consecutive business days, payment failure rate for migrated accounts within 0.5 percentage points of the old system's baseline failure rate, and finance/accounting sign-off on reconciliation accuracy.

**Description:** Migrate all remaining standard and mid-market accounts in controlled weekly waves, holding highest-ARR enterprise and contractually sensitive accounts for the final batch (Phase 4) so they benefit from maximum system maturity.

---

## Phase 4: Final Batch (High-Value & Enterprise Accounts)

**Percentage of users:** 10% (~4,000 users) — the highest-ARR, custom-contract, and enterprise accounts, migrated last

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with 100% of standard accounts migrated and stable for at least 14 calendar days, zero unresolved billing-accuracy incidents in that period, and dedicated account managers have individually confirmed contract terms (custom pricing, invoicing schedules, tax handling) are correctly mapped in the new system for each enterprise account.

**Description:** White-glove migration of remaining enterprise accounts with dedicated support monitoring for 30 days post-migration. The old billing system remains fully active and untouched during this phase to serve as a fallback and reconciliation reference. Decommissioning of the old system is explicitly out of scope for this phase and will only be planned and executed as a separate, subsequent initiative once all 40,000 users have been stable on the new system for at least 30 days.

---

## Halt Metrics (Numeric Thresholds)

- **Billing discrepancy rate:** If discrepancies between old-system and new-system calculated charges exceed **0.5% of migrated invoices** in any rolling 24-hour window, halt the rollout and freeze further migrations pending root-cause analysis.
- **Payment failure rate increase:** If payment failure rate for migrated accounts exceeds the pre-migration baseline by more than **2 percentage points**, halt the rollout.
- **Critical incident count:** If more than **2 P1 (critical) incidents** attributable to the new billing system occur within any 7-day period, halt the rollout.

---

## Risks

RISK: Billing calculation errors (incorrect charges, tax, or proration) cause customer financial harm | Run parallel dual-calculation reconciliation for every migrated account for at least 30 days and require finance sign-off before increasing migration percentage | Finance & Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Data migration errors corrupt or lose payment method, invoice history, or subscription data | Perform pre-migration data validation checksums and maintain read-only access to old system data for 90 days post full migration | Data Migration Engineering Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by migration-related tickets, delaying resolution and harming satisfaction | Staff a dedicated migration support queue with surge capacity and pre-written runbooks for top 10 anticipated issues before each phase begins | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated incorrectly, causing contractual disputes | Require manual account-manager verification of contract mapping for every enterprise account before Phase 4 migration | Enterprise Account Management Lead
RISK: Rollback from new system to old system fails or causes duplicate charges during the parallel-run period | Test and document rollback procedure in Phase 1 and re-validate it before each subsequent phase | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 4
